en: When two or three AI clients are open in one checkout, each of them can ask the shared server who else is there. A peer is a session: the server's own stdio client, every bridged majordomus mcp, and every client speaking /mcp directly. It is named by what its client sent in initialize (clientInfo.name and version), numbered p1, p2, ... in attachment order, with its transport, when it attached and when it was last seen. A client can announce one line of intent and the repository-relative paths it expects to touch; the others see it in majordomus_peers and in the instructions they get from initialize, which name the server's URL, the caller's own id and every other peer before the first tool call.
cs: Když jsou v jednom checkoutu otevřeni dva nebo tři AI klienti, každý se může sdíleného serveru zeptat, kdo další tam je. Peer je relace: vlastní stdio klient serveru, každý přemostěný majordomus mcp a každý klient mluvící přímo na /mcp. Je pojmenován tím, co jeho klient poslal v initialize (clientInfo.name a version), očíslován p1, p2, ... v pořadí připojení, s transportem, časem připojení a časem posledního spatření. Klient může oznámit jeden řádek záměru a cesty relativní k repozitáři, kterých se chce dotknout; ostatní to vidí v majordomus_peers a v instrukcích, které dostanou z initialize a které před prvním voláním nástroje jmenují URL serveru, vlastní id volajícího a každého dalšího peera.

en: A worker cannot be asked to record its own prompts. It never sees the bytes the person typed, only what the provider assembled from them, and a record written by a model is missing exactly the prompts that mattered: the first one of a session, which arrives before any instruction has been read, and every one where the model was busy doing what it was asked. An instruction in a bootstrap file is a request, not a mechanism, and there is no behavioural test that can prove a request was honoured.

en: The command line is the one interface that is declared twice — clap owns parsing, <t1/> and value sets, so <t2/> is a claim about a declaration that lives elsewhere rather than a projection built by walking the registry. The two are compared: <t3/> fails a capability that claims a command line the clap declaration does not answer (<t4/>) or answers only as a group that cannot be run (<t5/>), in <t6/>, in the crate's own tests, and as the <t7/> line of <t8/>, which exits 10. A runnable command that no capability claims is reported rather than refused — the process commands and the lifecycle verbs are legitimately hand-written, and the count is the measure of how much of the command line is still not derived — but it is never silent. Each such command says why it is local, once, in <t9/>, with one of four structural reasons and a note about that command in particular; <t10/> checks that statement in both directions, <t11/> carries the commands that carry none, and <t12/> exits 10 on the first of them. There is no inventory of such commands anywhere else: a list of names without reasons is a third copy of a set two declarations already pin, and the one this repository kept went stale twice before it was removed.

en: `brief.session` (CLI `majordomus brief`, `GET /api/v1/brief`, MCP `majordomus_brief`) answers one line and a multi-line form from the leaseholder's view: the command line asks the server its checkout's lease names and composes locally only when none answers, and a superseded server says that its own board is unreachable by the repository's gather. The Cockpit overview shows it. `session.brief_on_interval` switches a second provider mod, majordomus-brief, installed by `capture install` beside the handover mod: it renders the line as the status line on a clock, injects the multi-line brief into the conversation when the last one is older than the declared interval, and at session start tells the worker to schedule its own periodic self-report. ADR 0136 records the decision.
cs: `brief.session` (CLI `majordomus brief`, `GET /api/v1/brief`, MCP `majordomus_brief`) odpovídá jedním řádkem a víceřádkovou formou z pohledu držitele lease: příkazová řádka se ptá serveru, které lease jmenuje jeho checkout, a skládá lokálně, jen když neodpoví žádný, a překonaný server říká, že jeho vlastní nástěnka je pro sběr repozitáře nedosažitelná. Přehled Cockpitu ho ukazuje. `session.brief_on_interval` zapíná druhý provider mod, majordomus-brief, instalovaný příkazem `capture install` vedle modu handoveru: vykresluje řádek jako stavový řádek podle hodin, vkládá víceřádkový brief do konverzace, když je poslední starší než deklarovaný interval, a při startu relace říká workeru, aby si naplánoval vlastní pravidelné hlášení. ADR 0136 zaznamenává rozhodnutí.
